question: There are how many sectors are covered in Production linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme launched in August 2023?
solution:
The correct answer is __**14**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme** is an initiative by the Government of India to enhance domestic manufacturing and reduce dependence on imports.
 
• As of **August 2023**, the PLI Scheme covers **14 sectors**, which include critical industries such as electronics, pharmaceuticals, textiles, automobiles, and renewable energy.
 
• The scheme was launched with a **budgetary allocation** of approximately **₹1.97 lakh crore** over a 5-year period to incentivize manufacturers.
 
• The primary aim of the scheme is to boost the **Make in India** initiative and enhance India’s export potential by promoting advanced manufacturing capabilities.
 
• Some of the major sectors included in the PLI Scheme are **mobile and electronic components, pharmaceuticals, telecom, medical devices, textiles, specialty steel, and advanced chemistry cell batteries**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objective of the PLI Scheme:**

 
 
• The PLI Scheme is designed to **boost indigenous manufacturing**, attract investments, and promote the production of high-value products in India.
 
• It focuses on enhancing the **global competitiveness** of Indian manufacturers by providing financial incentives based on incremental production.
 
• The scheme aims to create a robust ecosystem for the development of advanced manufacturing industries and generate **employment opportunities**.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the PLI Scheme:**
 
 
• The scheme offers **incentives ranging from 4% to 6%** of the incremental sales of goods manufactured in India.
 
• It seeks to **reduce import dependency** and improve the quality of domestic products to meet international standards.
 
• Under the scheme, sectors like **semiconductors and renewable energy** are given special emphasis to align with India’s vision for a sustainable future.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Sectors Covered:**
 
 
• **Mobile Manufacturing:** India has emerged as a global hub for mobile manufacturing under the PLI Scheme, with companies like Apple and Samsung setting up production units.
 
• **Pharmaceuticals:** The scheme has contributed to the development of **bulk drugs and key starting materials (KSMs)** to reduce dependency on imports from countries like China.
 
• **Textiles:** Focuses on **man-made fibers** and technical textiles, aiming to position India as a major player in the global textile industry.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Scheme:**
 
 
• The PLI Scheme is expected to **generate employment** for millions of people and significantly contribute to India’s GDP.
 
• It has boosted **foreign direct investment (FDI)** in key sectors, with global companies showing interest in setting up operations in India.
 
• Several industries have reported a **significant increase in production capacity** and export volumes due to the scheme’s implementation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Budgetary Allocation:**

 
 
• The total outlay for the PLI Scheme is approximately **₹1.97 lakh crore**, distributed across 14 sectors.
 
• Each sector has been allocated a specific budget based on its potential to contribute to India’s economic growth and self-reliance.
 
 
 
• **Role of State Governments:**
 
 
• State governments play a crucial role in facilitating the implementation of the PLI Scheme by providing **infrastructure support, land, and other resources**.
 
• Many states have introduced their own incentives to complement the central PLI Scheme and attract investments.
 
 
 
• **Global Recognition:**
 
 
• The PLI Scheme has positioned India as a **preferred manufacturing destination** for global investors, particularly in sectors like electronics and renewable energy.
 
• It has helped India improve its **ease of doing business** rankings and attract high-tech industries.
 
 

b1
